findings.obligation: L5: the issue page holds exactly one description region, present whether or not text is stored (acceptance S1 P3 row: an issue with nothing written down still has one place for it).
findings.observation: The region is located by keeping EVERY element whose collected text equals the stored description, then asserting the count is 1. In a wrapper implementation such as a div of class issue-description holding a p that holds the stored text, both the div and the p collect exactly that text and nothing else, so the count is 2 and the scenario reds against a correct page. The same equality then fixes the shape (tag plus exact class string) that the empty page is searched for, so an empty state that keeps the region but carries the shipped empty class, as the attachment and comment empty states do, also reds.
findings.remediation: Keep only the INNERMOST matches: drop any candidate that contains another candidate, then assert the count is 1. For the empty page, match the region by its tag and by the presence of the same class rather than by exact class-string equality, so a correct implementation is not forced into one incidental markup shape.

findings.obligation: L6 declares its generator domain as arbitrary unicode description text including right-to-left text, and declares that each drawn text is an observation of the law.
findings.observation: The drawn alphabet holds markup characters, quotes, backtick, whitespace, latin letters, one Greek letter, one CJK character, brackets and digits; it holds no right-to-left character, so the declared domain is not drawn from. Drawn lengths start at 1 (gen_range 1..=120), and the reading is page-text CONTAINMENT, so a one- or two-character drawn text occurs elsewhere in the served document anyway and that case cannot falsify a page that shows no description at all. The four named texts still falsify, so the scenario as a whole holds; the short draws add no observation.
findings.remediation: Add at least one right-to-left character to the alphabet, and raise the minimum drawn length so every drawn text is a distinct observation of the law rather than an incidental substring of the page.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/ui-bare-pages.feature:85-90, scenario: The page and the overlay advertise the same shortcuts
findings.obligation: A RED-trigger comment in the oracle states why the scenario fails before the behaviour exists, so a crafter can tell intentional RED from a broken reading.
findings.observation: The comment says the page arm advertises nothing at all today. It does advertise: today every client is given the same fragment, which carries the seven shipped rows, so this scenario is GREEN at RED time and is one of the three greens the host measured. The scenario is sound as a drift guard once the page arm exists; only its stated reason is wrong, and a crafter who trusts it would read the green as a defect of the lane.
findings.remediation: Reword the comment: both arms are the same body today, so this reading is green until the page arm exists, and it then holds the line against a page that writes a list of its own.

findings.location: docs/feature/ui-bare-pages/acceptance.md, slice S1, the P1 row whose stimulus reads: follows the nav to the keyboard shortcut list at desk width, and opens the same list on a 390 by 844 phone
findings.obligation: Every acceptance row names the locator of every test that covers it, so each obligation is traceable to its falsifier.
findings.observation: The row names both widths, and the oracle carries both scenarios (Opening the shortcut list from the nav, each key sits beside what it does; On her phone each shortcut key still sits beside what it does), but the disposition names the desk scenario alone. The phone reading, which is what expectation E2 asks for, is covered yet untraceable from the brief.
findings.remediation: Name the phone scenario in that row's disposition beside the desk one.

findings.location: docs/feature/ui-bare-pages/architecture.md, Failures B1 and B2: the issue page second projection read answers nothing, or errors
findings.obligation: Each declared failure mode gets an observation that distinguishes it from every other mode: B1 must serve the shipped uniform not-found page, never a page with an empty title or a blank status; B2 must take the shipped internal-error path.
findings.observation: The oracle drives the public HTTP routes only. The gap between the handler resolution and the projection read is internal to one request, so no public stimulus makes the second read answer nothing while the first succeeded, and the design declares no other locator for these two refusals. Both are uncovered, and a half-filled issue page would ship green.
findings.remediation: Declare the observation locator for B1 and B2, a foundry-app test of show_issue over a projection read that answers nothing and one that errors, as a completion obligation of this feature; or record them as refusals this Request does not observe. This does not block craft and stays open until completion.

findings.location: docs/feature/ui-bare-pages/architecture.md, law L6, Treatment Broad: the repository generated-test library with its own seeded runs and its persisted failure file, and library shrinking on the generated string
findings.obligation: The declared treatment of a broad law must be the one the oracle can build in the native crate.
findings.observation: crates/foundry-acceptance declares no property-test library, so the oracle draws 24 texts from StdRng at the fixed seed 20261121, reports the shortest offending text with its seed and index, and persists no failure file. The law is still read over the declared named texts and the drawn ones, but the declared library, its seeded-run record and its shrinking are not what runs.
findings.remediation: Record the deviation in the L6 treatment (fixed seed 20261121, 24 drawn texts, shortest-offender reporting instead of library shrinking, no persisted failure file), or add the generated-test dependency to the acceptance crate and restate the treatment. Non-blocking for craft.

findings.obligation: L2: both answers advertise exactly the shipped rows, each key paired with what it does, in the shipped order.
findings.observation: The pairing is built by zipping every [data-shortcut] element of the body with every dd element of the whole body, in document order. On the framed page arm any other definition list the card frame or the page heading introduces shifts every pair by one and reds a correct page, and a shorter dd run is silently truncated by the zip rather than reported as a broken pairing. The browser reading of the same rows already pairs each key with its own next sibling.
findings.remediation: Pair each key with its own following sibling, as the browser reading does, and report a key whose meaning is missing instead of dropping the pair.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_ui_bare_pages.rs:830 elements_of_shape, with the shape taken at description_area_shape
findings.obligation: L5: the description region is present on the page of an issue with nothing written down, and there is exactly one of it (the same obligation as the corrected finding).
findings.observation: The class reading is now presence rather than an exact string, which closes the shipped empty-class case. One residual path remains: when the innermost element carrying the description has no class of its own, the shape is the tag with an empty class list, and the all-of-the-wanted-classes test is then vacuously true, so EVERY element of that tag on the empty page is counted. With a wrapper implementation such as a classed div holding a bare p, the shape becomes p with no class, and the empty issue page already carries a timeline-empty paragraph and a comments-empty paragraph, so the count is three and a correct page reds. A description area that carries its own class, which the stylesheet rules this Request adds would give it, is read correctly.
findings.remediation: When the innermost carrying element has no class, take the nearest ancestor that carries one as the shape, so the place is always identified by something the page itself declares; alternatively refuse an empty shape with a message naming it as a defect of the reading rather than of the page. Non-blocking: the implementation the design describes carries a class.

observations.text: Re-review of the correction delta only, at HEAD ac96408 with a clean worktree. argv: git diff --name-only e1949a1..HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance docs/feature/ui-bare-pages (exit 0): the support file, the feature file, acceptance.md and architecture.md with their rendered twins and the handoff. No lane was run: the author supplied a run at these same bytes (ui-bare-pages 39 scenarios, 3 passed, 36 failed, 183 steps, 147 passed; clippy -D warnings and fmt check exit 0), the scenario and step counts are unchanged from the accepted revision, and nothing outside the delta moved. This cites that run; it is not a new execution. Unaffected judgments from the accepted review are retained.

Four of the five oracle findings are closed. The shortcut pairing now reads each key with its own next element sibling and gives a key with nothing after it an empty meaning, so a body that writes more keys than meanings reds as the short run it is instead of being cut to the shorter list, and a page built from a different row markup is no longer punished for it. The description area now keeps the innermost matches only, so a wrapper and the line inside it count as one place. The drawn alphabet carries Hebrew and Arabic letters, so the declared right-to-left domain is drawn from, and DESCRIPTION_MIN_LEN = 24 makes every drawn text long enough to be a reading of its own; the seed, the case count and the four named texts are unchanged. The drift-guard comment now states plainly that the reading is green today because both ways of asking get one body, and what it holds from the moment the page arm exists. Both design findings are recorded, and the record is honest rather than a promise. B1 and B2 now name the handler, the read, the shipped refusal body and the shipped internal-error helper, and state that each is UNOBSERVED by this Request with the reason: the gap is a race between two reads inside one request, the driving port cannot hold it open, and the handler takes the concrete store, so a test would have to invent a seam that is production design this Request does not hold; the residual risk row Y6 carries it. L6's treatment now names what actually runs: no generated-test library in the acceptance crate, StdRng at the fixed seed 20261121, 24 draws per run, no persisted failure file, and shortest-offending-text reporting in place of library shrinking, with the limit stated - a smaller counterexample outside the drawn set is not searched for. Both remain completion obligations, not closed observations.
